newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman says it joined WIPO, hopes to help investment.
newsitem.headline: Oman says it joined WIPO, hopes to help investment.

text.p: Oman said on Monday it has joined the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) and hoped the move would help attract more foreign investment in the Gulf Arab state.

Commerce and Industry Minister Makboul bin Ali bin Sultan told a conference on intellectual property rights in Muscat that Oman joined the WIPO in September and has applied to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
He said joining WIPO "will have positive effects on the general investment climate in the sultanate and will boost the credibility of our foreign trade and investment transactions."
WIPO overseas worldwide protection of intellectual property rights and cooperates with countries developing such laws.
Oman, a small independent oil producer, introduced copyright laws in June this year as part of its efforts to attract foreign investors and help diversify and develop its economy.
Analysts say the sectors dominated by pirated goods in Oman were computer software, audio and video material, followed by consumer goods.
U.S. software makers estimate their annual losses to piracy in Oman at around $10 million.
